elements.element: No obligation on Customer to use Vendor as sole/exclusive supplier
elements.evidence: 7.2 as revised imposes no exclusivity: "Customer need not disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer"; no sole-supplier duty appears in the clause

elements.element: No disclose-competing-offer obligation on Customer (de facto right of first refusal)
elements.evidence: "Customer need not disclose or match" replaces "Customer must disclose and match"

elements.element: No match-the-offer obligation on Customer before engaging another provider
elements.evidence: "need not disclose or match ... any more favourable commercial offer it receives"

elements.element: Customer free to engage another provider without precondition
elements.evidence: "Before engaging another provider, Customer need not disclose or match" — the precondition is removed

elements.element: Any exclusivity limited to a defined product category
elements.evidence: No exclusivity of any scope remains after the edit, so no category limit is needed
No exclusivity term exists to limit

elements.element: Automatic termination of exclusivity on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates
elements.evidence: Condition demonstrably absent — no exclusivity obligation subsists in Section 7.2

reasons: The single replace operation flips only the operative verb phrase ("must disclose and match" → "need not disclose or match"), eliminating the de facto right of first refusal and thereby meeting the preferred position of no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer.

Minimality is satisfied: a short operator/verb-phrase substitution was used rather than a clause rewrite, and no fallback-only mechanics (category scope, 12-month cap, SLA-failure termination) were imported.

Intent is preserved: the surrounding sentence structure and the remainder of the Agreement (including Section 12.3's no-exclusivity acknowledgement) remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced. The residual lead-in "Before engaging another provider" is now merely descriptive but creates no contradiction.
